“14. We have already extracted section 25B since its amendment and the change in language is the legislative 
exposition of which note must be taken. In fact, we need not further dilate upon this aspect because in Surendra 
Kumar Verma_and Ors. vy. Central Government Industrial-cum-Labour Court, New Delhi and Anr., Chinnappa 
Reddy. J., after noticing the amendment and referring to the decision in Sur_Enamel_and Stamping Works (P)

"These changes brought about by Act 36 of 1964 appear to be clearly designed to provide that a Workman who has 
actually worked under the employer for not less than 240 days during a period of twelve months shall be deemed to 
have been in continuous service for a period of one year whether or not he has in fact been in such continuous service 
for a period of one year. It is enough that he has worked for 240 days in a period of 12 months, it is not necessary that 
he should have been in the service of the employer for one whole year." 


In a concurring judgment Pathak J. agreed with this interpretation of section 25B(2). Therefore, both on principle 
and on precedent it must be held that section 25B(2) comprehends a situation where a Workman is not in employment 
for a period of 12 calendar months, but has rendered service for a period of 240 days within the period of 12 
calendar months commencing and counting backwards from the relevant date, i.e. the date of retrenchment. If he has, 
he would be deemed to be in continuous service for a period of one year for the purpose of section 25B and 
Chapter VA.”

“Till 1982, the branches of the appellant Bank in Calcutta region were recruiting persons locally to work as

contained in the writ petition was thus misconceived and therefore the learned single Judge and the Division Bench, 
when it first decided the appeal, were right in dismissing the writ petition and the appeal respectively.”

Supreme Court have has laid down principle regarding regularization of the Workman on permanent posts. Hon’ble 
Supreme Court have laid down the prepositions of regularization of the workmen to permanent post is as under: - 


“(i) Wide as they are, the powers of the Labour Court and the Industrial Court cannot extend to a direction to order 
regularisation, where such a direction would in the context of public employment offend the provisions contained 
in Article 14 of the Constitution; 


(ii) The statutory power of the Labour Court or Industrial Court to grant relief to workmen including the status of 
permanency continues to exist in circumstances where the employer has indulged in an unfair labour practice by not 
filling up permanent posts even though such posts are available and by continuing to employ workmen as temporary 
or daily wage employees despite their performing the same work as regular workmen on lower wages; 


(iii) The power to create permanent or sanctioned posts lies outside the judicial domain and where no posts are 
available, a direction to grant regularisation would be impermissible merely on the basis of the number of years of 
service; 


(iv) Where an employer has regularised similarly situated workmen either in a scheme or otherwise, it would be open 
to workmen who have been deprived of the same benefit at par with the workmen who have been regularised to make 
a complaint before the Labour or Industrial Court, since the deprivation of the benefit would amount to a violation of 
Article 14; and 


(v) In order to constitute an unfair labour practice under Section 2(ra) read with Item 10 of the Vth Schedule of the 
ID Act, the employer should be engaging workmen as badlis, temporaries or casuals, and continuing them for years, 
with the object of depriving them of the benefits payable to permanent workmen.

In the case of Mahboob Deepak vs. Nagar Panchayat Gajraula & Anr, Civil Appeal No.5875/2007 date of 
judgement 13.12.2007, Hon’ble Supreme Court have held:- 


“8. Respondent is a Local Authority. The terms and conditions of employment of the employees are governed by a 
Statute and statutory rules. No appointment can be made by a Local Authority without following the provisions of the 
recruitment rules. Any appointment made in violation of the said rules as also the constitutional scheme of equality as 
contained in Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India would be a nullity. 


9. Due to some exigency of work, although recruitment on daily wages or on an ad hoc basis was permissible, but by 
reason thereof an employee cannot claim any right to be permanently absorbed in service or made permanent in 
absence of any statute or statutory rules. Merely because an employee has completed 240 days of work in a year

permanent vacancy and even though the 2" Respondent was appointed on temporary basis, his services were not 
liable to be terminated and he was to be regularised into service on permanent basis. Shastry award warrants that no 
temporary appointment can be made to a permanent post. But the matter is now covered by two division bench 
judgements dated 28.11.1986 in W.A. No.791 of 1986 and 25.8.1987 in W.A. No.270 of 1982. The ratio decided in the 
two judgements is to the effect that there cannot be any mandate to appoint employees on permanent basis when the 
requirement was for appointment on temporary basis. But it is held in the said judgements that when a temporary 
appointee is ousted from service and not for misconduct and, if again temporary appointment is to be made, then, the 
case of such temporary appointee who was ousted, has got to be considered in accordance with Sec. 25-H of 
the Act.” 


In the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Piara Singh and others. 1992 (4) SCC 118, therein Hon’ble 
Supreme Court have held:- 


“49. If for any reason an adhoc or temporary employee is continued for a fairly long spell, the authorities must 
consider his case for regularization provided he is eligible and qualified according to the rules and his service record 
is satisfactory and his appointment does not run counter to the reservation policy of the state.” 


In the above cited judgements by the Workman the facts of the case are different hence do not apply to instant case 
of Workman. 


47. Thus, in view of fore gone discussion and laws laid down by Hon’ble Apex Court as discussed above, the 
claim of workman of regularization in the employment of Respondent is not substantiated by the evidence of 
Petitioner, WW1 in her cross examination has admitted that she is not aware of any settlements and she is not having 
any document to show that any person who worked for less number of days than him was given appointment in the 
bank and she has no document to show that any of her juniors is continuing in service of the bank as of now. 
Therefore, the claim of the Petitioner for regularization in the employment of Respondent bank is not tenable. 
Further, Petitioner failed to produce any document in evidence to establish that any temporary employee junior to 
him is working in the Respondent bank. Therefore, Petitioner is not entitled for regularization in the service of the 
Respondent. 


This point is answered against the Petitioner Workman and in favour of the Respondent. 


48. Point No.IV:- In view of the discussion and finding given at Point Nos. I, II and III, the Workman is not 
entitled for any relief and claim statement of Workman sans merit and liable to be dismissed. 


This Point is answered accordingly. 
AWARD 


In view of the fore gone discussion, it is held that the action of the Respondent bank in terminating the 
services of Smt. A. Mahendra Mani, Ex. Messenger by way of oral orders w.e.f. 1.4.1997 is justified. Hence, the 
Petitioner is not entitled for any relief as prayed for. 


Award is passed accordingly. Transmit.

ID 15/2017

registered as ID No. 15/2017 and due notices were issued to both the parties for their appearance fixing the case to

the reference. Even then, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner was once again directed to appear and to file claim 
statement fixing the case to 03.08.2026. The Petitioner did not turn up nor was any authorized representative of the

In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of sub-section (1) and sub —section (2A) of Section 10 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947) Government Of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its Order No. L- 
20012/123/2015-IR(CM-I) dated 03/11/2015 has been pleased to refer the following dispute between the employer 1.6. 
management of Lodna Area of M/s. BCCL, Dhanbad and their workman through Secretary, Jharkhand Janta Mazdoor 
Union, Dhanbad for adjudication by this Tribunal: 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of Lodna Colliery of M/s BCCL in dismissing, Shri Anil 
Kumar Paswan, Ex-SDL Mazdoor, Pers No. 02835957 from the services of the company vide order dated 
03.07.2010 is justified and fair? If not, to what relief the concerned workman is entitled?” 


2. The case of the workman as per the written statement filed on his behalf is that Sri Anil Kumar Paswan was 
a permanent employee of Lodna Colliery working as SDL Mazdoor and keeping unblemished record of service who 
was falsely implicated in a criminal case and was sent in jail custody w.e.f. 27.07.2006 to 07.02.2014. The wife of 
Anil Kumar Paswan informed the management that her husband Anil Kumar Paswan is in jail custody since 
27.07.2006. As per the Circular of the management if a workman is in jail custody in connection with criminal case he 
is liable for suspension during the period he is in jail custody. Although the management was having full knowledge 
that the workman concerned is in jail custody even then the management has not suspended him just to deprive him 
from the subsistence allowance. Despite the knowledge of jail custody of the workman, charge sheet was issued 
against him which was received by his wife. After receiving the same his wife requested the management not to take 
any disciplinary action against him till he is in jail custody. Without serving chargesheet to the workman concerned the 
management conducted ex-parte enquiry and dismissed him vide dismissal letter dated 24.06/03.07.2010 for 
unauthorized absence. After release from the jail custody Anil Kumar Paswan reported for duty but he was not allowed 
to resume his duty as such he raised industrial dispute through the union but the conciliation proceeding was ended in 
failure that led to reference of this case. The workman concerned never absented from his duty unauthorisedly, 
actually he was in jail custody and due to the same he was prevented from attending his duty as it was beyond his 
control. He has not committed any misconduct. He was never served any charge sheet. The report of the Enquiry 
Officer is perverse. The enquiry conducted is not fair and proper and not as per the Principle of Natural Justice so the 
dismissal of the workman is liable to be set aside and at last it was prayed to reinstate the workman with full back 
wages. 


3. On the other hand the case of the management as per the written statement cum rejoinder filed on its behalf 
is that Sri Anil Kumar Paswan, Ex-SDL Mazdoor of Lodna Colliery had been absenting unauthorizedly from the 
services of the company w.e.f. 24.07.2006. A charge sheet was issued against him vide No. 116 dated 31.12.2007 
under clause 26.1.1 of the provision of the Certified Standing Orders of the company and he was allowed 7 days time 
to submit his written explanation and the charge sheet was sent at his permanent address too by Regd. Post but his wife 
Smt. Pinki Devi intimated that her husband is in jail. The Disciplinary Authority had got the matter enquired by 
appointing the Enquiry Officer and the M.R. The notices were issue to the above named workman for appearance and 
his wife was also given opportunity to produce papers regarding the above matter about his being in jail custody. The 
Central Jail, Dhanbad was also approached about the position of the above named workman and the Superintendent, 
Central Jail, Dhanbad vide his letter No. 767 dated 26.04.2010 had intimated to the Project Officer, Lodna Colliery 
that the workman has been convicted in GR Case No. 1362/99 under Section 452, 302, 149, 307, 148, 325, 323 for life 
imprisonment by the court of Addl. Session Judge FTC II on 27.07.2006 and presently he is in the Jail Custody as 
convict. Thereafter the Enquiry Officer held the enquiry and submitted the enquiry report. The Second Show Cause 
Notice vide No. 776 dated 11/19.06.2010 allowing 7 days time for submitting reply was also sent. The matter was 
considered and the Disciplinary Authority had decided to dismiss the workman concerned and dismissal order was 
passed vide letter No. 89 dated 24.06/08.07.2016. This industrial dispute was raised and reply to the same was 
submitted before the Assistant Labour Commissioner (C) Dhanbad. The conciliation was held but the same ended in 
failure that led to the reference of this case. On the basis of the proved misconduct and also that he was convicted in 
the criminal case for life imprisonment it is felt that the action of the management is just, fair and proper in dismissing 
the concerned employee. In case the enquiry is found not fair and proper, the management may be allowed to lead the 
evidence to prove his case and submit documents. By way of rejoinder the stand taken by the workman has been 
denied and the action of the management in holding enquiry and dismissal of the workman has been submitted to be 
fair and reasonable. 


4. The workman has also filed a separate rejoinder dated 15.07.2016 to the W/S of the management in which 
at the very beginning the stand taken by the management has been denied by the workman submitting that the 
management has not issued any charge sheet under Clause 26.1.19 of the Certified Standing Orders and the enquiry of 
the Enquiry Officer is perverse as he was having full knowledge that the workman was in jail custody and he was not 
attending duty the same being beyond his control.

5. Issue 


“Whether the action of the management of Lodna Colliery of M/s BCCL in dismissing, Shri Anil Kumar 
Paswan, Ex-SDL Mazdoor, Pers No. 02835957 from the services of the company vide order dated 03.07.2010 is 
justified and fair? If not, to what relief the concerned workman is entitled?” 


6. It is relevant to mention that on the preliminary point the management examined MW-1 Jogendra Kumar 
Biruli and got exhibited the following documents: 


Exhibit M-1 — Copy of Charge Sheet dated 31.12.2006 

Exhibit M-2 — Copy of Reply to the Charge Sheet 

Exhibit M-3 — Copy of Office Order dated 20.01.2009 appointing the E.O. and M.R 

Exhibit M-4 Series — Copy of Notice of Enquiry dated 28.01.2009 and 09.04.2009 

Exhibit M-5 — Copy of Application of Smt. Pinki Devi received on 11.02.2009 

Exhibit M-6 — Copy of Enquiry Proceedings 

Exhibit M-7 — Copy of Note Sheet dated 06/08.05.2009 

Exhibit M-8 — Copy of Letter dated 26.04.2010 from the Superintendent Central Jail, Dhanbad 
Exhibit M-9 — Copy of Note Sheet dated 26.02.2010 

Exhibit M-10 — Copy of Second Show Cause Notice 


Exhibit M-11 — Copy of Letter dated 15.04.2010 from P.O., Lodna Colliery to the Jail Superintendent, 
Dhanbad. 


7. The workman also examined WW-1 Anil Kumar Paswan. 


8. After hearing both sides on the preliminary point the enquiry proceeding conducted Ex-parte was held as 
not fair the same being against the Principles of Natural Justice. 


9. Thereafter the management was provided opportunities to adduce evidence to prove his case and in 
furtherance of the same the management examined MW-2 Abhijeet Kumar. 


10. The workman again examined himself and got exhibited the following documents. 
Exhibit W-1 — Photo copy of Identity Card issued by the BCCL 

Exhibit W-2 — Copy of Charge sheet dated 31.12.2006 

Exhibit W-3 — Intimation by his wife Smt. Pinki Devi dated 09.02.2009 

Exhibit W-4 — Copy of dismissal order dated 24.06.2010 

Exhibit W-5 — Copy of application of rejoining dated 31.01.2015 


Exhibit W-6 — Copy of Letter dated 11.03.2014 issued from Office Superintendent L.J.N, Central Jail, 
Hazaribagh 


Exhibit W-7 — Application dated 13.02.2015 given by the concerned workman for rejoining 
Exhibit W-8 — Copy of Judgment and Order of conviction in ST No. 167 of 2000 dated 24.07.2006 
Exhibit W-9 — Copy of Certified Standing Orders 

Exhibit W-10 — Copy of ID. Card 

11. Heard both sides and perused the materials on record. 


12. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the workman has submitted that the workman was a permanent employee of 
BCCL and on 24.07.2006 he remained absent from his duty because in a family dispute he was falsely sent to jail and 
he remained in jail custody from 27.07.2006 to 07.02.2014. His wife had given information of his being in jail custody 
to the BCCL management and despite that he was illegally charge sheeted on 31.12.2006 that was not received by the 
workman though his wife Pinki Devi gave written reply on 15.01.2007 to the management informing that he was 
detained in Dhanbad Jail in a family dispute and after being acquitted from the same he would return to this duty. 
Again on 09.02.2009 his wife gave information regarding his jail custody to the management but the enquiry was not 
deferred. He has neither received any charge sheet nor notice of enquiry nor an opportunity to defend his case which is 
against the principles of natural justice and on 24.06.2010 he was illegally dismissed from his service which is against 
the provisions of Certified standing Order. He was not absent deliberately rather he was in jail custody and therefore 
the charge of unauthorized absence is not proved. Against the conviction he has preferred appeal wherefrom he has 


9946 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : AUGUST 29, 2026/ BHADRA 7, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


been bailed out. He has not committed any misconduct. It was further submitted that the workman’s dismissal is illegal 
because he was appointed by the General manager whereas he was dismissed by the project officer who is lower in 
rank and prayed to set aside the dismissal order and reinstate his service without back wages. 


13. On the other hand the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the management has submitted that the workman had 
become disentitled to continue in service because of his conviction and sentence of life imprisonment. The conviction 
of life imprisonment itself constitutes independent misconduct. Once the fact of conviction came to the knowledge of 
the management through the Jail Superintendent the employer was empowered to terminate his services under clause 
26.1.19 of the Certified Standing Order and for that separate domestic enquiry is not necessary. The employer is not 
expected to keep a convicted employee. Release on bail does not wipe out the conviction unless conviction itself is set 
aside by the Appellate Court. It has further been submitted that the conviction and sentence are undisputed. Hence, 
absence of separate charge sheet under clause 26.1.19 is not fatal. Conviction for serious criminal offence for life 
imprisonment destroys confidence and employer cannot be compelled to retain such employee. The misconduct 
against the workman is well proved and the dismissal order passed by the Disciplinary Authority against the workman 
is quite in accordance with law and prayed to answer the reference accordingly. 


14. As the enquiry has already been held as unfair due to being held in absence of the workman Ex-parte, this 
is the duty of the management to prove his case by independent and additional evidence by way of de novo trial and in 
that sequence the management has examined MW Abhijeet Kumar on 18.12.25 who has appeared before the Court to 
adduce his evidence on the basis of the perusal of the office record and in his examination- in- chief he has admitted 
that Anil Kumar Paswan was working as SDL Mazdoor and he was issued charge sheet vide letter dated 24.07.2006 
for being absent without information to which the reply was given by his wife and she had informed that her husband 
was in jail custody. Management had written letter to the Dhanbad Jailer who had given reply intimating reason and 
charges for his jail detention. He has further stated that if a workman is found guilty that comes under the category of 
serious misconduct and if he is serving the life imprisonment, he need not continue in the company and after receiving 
the information he was immediately dismissed from his service. In cross-examination he has admitted that he has no 
personal knowledge of this case because he was not in job at that time. The workman Anil Kumar Paswan was 
appointed by General Manager but he was dismissed by Project Manager. General Manager’s rank is higher to that of 
the Project Manager. He does not remember if the charge sheet issued against him had mentioned regarding the 
criminal case or not. 


15. Besides this oral evidence the management has not adduced any documentary independent or additional 
evidence to prove the charges against the workman. 


16. On the other hand the workman Anil Kumar Paswan has examined himself on 1.04.26 as WW in support 
of his case in which he has detailed his case and admitted that he was a permanent employee of BCCL and on 
24.07.2006 he remained absent from his duty because in a family dispute he was falsely sent to jail and he remained in 
jail custody from 27.07.2006 to 07.02.2014. His wife had given information of his being in jail custody to the BCCL 
management and despite that information he was illegally charge sheeted on 31.12.2006 that was not received by him 
though his wife Pinki Devi gave written reply on 15.01.2007 to the management informing that he was detained in 
Dhanbad Jail in a family dispute and after being acquitted from the same he would return to this duty. Again on 
09.02.2009 his wife gave information regarding his jail custody to the management but the enquiry was not deferred. 
He has neither received any charge sheet nor notice of enquiry nor an opportunity to present his case which is against 
the natural justice and on 24.06.2010 he was illegally dismissed from his service by the project officer who is not the 
disciplinary authority under the provisions of Certified standing Order. He was not absent deliberately rather he was in 
jail custody whereas he was charge sheeted under clause 26.1.1 for being absent from duty. He was not charge sheeted 
for conviction so his dismissal on that ground is illegal. Against the conviction he has preferred appeal where from he 
has been bailed out. He has not committed any misconduct and prayed to set aside the dismissal order and reinstate his 
service. He has also submitted documents that were marked Ext.W-1 to Ext.W-10. In cross-examination he has stated 
that on 24.07.2006 he was absent from his duty without taking any leave for which the company had issued charge 
sheet against him. He had not given any reply of the same but his wife had given reply of the same by writing a letter 
to the management on 15.01.2007 that her husband was in jail custody. Thereafter BCCL had given notice of enquiry 
for 28.0102009 that was received by his wife. Then on 9.02.2009 she again gave a letter to management that her 
husband was in jail custody but reason and period was not mentioned therein. He was convicted under section 302 
IPC. He was on bail and appeal is pending. 


17. The workman has also submitted the documentary evidence out of which Exhibit W-1 and Exhibit W- 
10 both are the copies of Identity Card issued in the name of the workman Anil Kumar Paswan by the BCCL, Lodna 
Area. Exhibit W-2 is the copy of charge sheet dated 31.12.2006 in which the workman has been issued the charge 
sheet under clause 26.1.1 of the Certified Standing Order for misconduct ie habitual late attendance or willful or 
habitual absence from the duty without sufficient cause and this also contains the attendance of the previous 3 years 
i.e. 2005, 2004 and 2003 but in none of these years any absence or punishment is reported/recorded against the 
workman. Exhibit W-3 is the letter given by his wife Pinki Devi dated 09.02.2009 that has been submitted before the 
Enquiry Officer in reply to the charge sheet informing that she had already informed in writing on 15.01.2007 
regarding her husband and requested to stay the proceeding till final judgment. Exhibit W-4 is the dismissal letter

dated 24.06/03.07.2010 passed by the Project Officer, Lodna Colliery which says that the workman was absenting 
since 24.07.2006 unauthorizedly and without information or satisfactory reason and consequently vide order dated 
31.12.2006 charge sheet was issued against him by Manager, Lodna Colliery that was sent at his permanent address 
through registered post and reply of the same was filed by his wife Pinki Devi on 15.01.2007 stating that he was 
detained in Dhanbad Jail since 24.07.2006 and thereafter no further information was received. The Enquiry Officer 
and management representative were appointed for holding domestic enquiry that was held on 09.02.2009, 02.03.2009 
and 20.04.2009 but he remained absent. His wife Pinki Devi was also given opportunity to submit the explanation. 
Thereafter the information was also collected from the Dhanbad Jail wherefrom vide letter dated 26.04.2010 it was 
informed that the workman was under life imprisonment by the order of the Court and seeing the seriousness of the 
situation he also deeply perused the enquiry report submitted by the Enquiry Officer and ultimately he reached the 
conclusion that his case was fit for dismissal from the services of the company and so he was dismissed from the 
service of the company with immediate effect. Exhibit W-5 and Exhibit W-7 are the application given by the 
workman Anil Kumar Paswan after being released on bail on 07.02.2014, one to the Project Officer, Lodna Colliery 
and other to the General Manager, Lodna Area No. 10, BCCL. Exhibit W-6 is a type of Certificate issued by the 
Superintendent Jaiprakash Narayan, Central Jail, Hazaribagh with detailed information of the session case and charges 
against the workman informing that he has been sentenced by the Court of Additional sessions Judge, FTC II, 
Dhanbad on 27.07.2006 and on 03.07.2011 he was transferred to Central Jail, Hazaribagh as convicted prisoner and on 
07.02.2024 he was released on bail. Exhibit W-8 is the copy of the judgment of conviction and order of sentence 
dated 24.07.2006 passed by the Additional Session Judge, F.T.C. H, Dhanbad in S.T. No. 167 of 2000 which shows 
that the workman has convicted for the offence of murder inter-alia and sentenced to Rigorous Life Imprisonment etc. 
Exhibit W-9 is the copy of different clauses of the Certified Standing Order of establishment under BCCL and on its 
perusal it transpires that as per Clause 26.1.1, act of misconduct shall include habitual late attendance or wilful or 
habitual absence from duty without sufficient cause and as per Clause 26.1.19, act of misconduct shall include 
conviction by a Court of law for any criminal offence involving moral turpitude and Clause 27.2.6 says that no order 
of discharge or dismissal from service shall be made by an authority lower than the appointing authority of the 
workman. 


18. On perusal of the charge sheet it transpires that the workman has been issued charge sheet under clause 
26.1.1 of Certified Standing Order of BCCL for misconduct ie habitual late attendance or willful or habitual absence 
from duty without sufficient cause but the management has failed to adduce any evidence to prove this charge of 
habitual late attendance because the same charge sheet dated 31.12.2006 also contains the attendance of previous 3 
years of the workman in which neither any period of absence nor previous punishment imposed if any, has been 
recorded and as regards the willful absence from duty, admittedly the workman remained absent from duty since 
24.07.2006 due to his conviction in Session Trial No. 167 of 2000 (Exhibit W-8) and consequent detention prior to 
07.02.2014 when he was released on bail (Exhibit W-6) and so his absence is not willful rather due to compelling 
reasons of his imprisonment by the order of the Court of law that was beyond his control and therefore the charge of 
habitual late attendance or willful or habitual absence from duty without sufficient cause is held as not proved by the 
management with the help of sufficient documentary evidence. Not only this, the management also failed to produce 
the service record or attendance register or any other document showing pre-existing habitual absenteeism prior to the 
jail sentence and therefore his absence does not amount to punishable misconduct for want of intention. 


19. Now as regards the dismissal order dated 24.06/03.07.2010, on its perusal it is evident that the Project 
Officer while passing the order of dismissal has even considered the conviction order of the Court together with the 
enquiry report submitted by the Enquiry Officer but without issuing any revised charge sheet under Clause 26.1.19 of 
the Certified Standing Order which is also serious infirmity because without a specific charge sheet, no one can be 
held guilty and the dismissal order cannot be based on the same. 


20. Additionally, on perusal of the copy of appointment letter that is available on the case record though not 
exhibited from the side of the workman it appears that the General Manager of Lodna Area is the Appointing 
Authority of the workman whereas his dismissal order shows that he has been dismissed by the Project Officer, Lodna 
Colliery who is lower in rank which has also been admitted by MW Abhijeet Kumar in paragraph 14 & 15 of his 
cross-examination and this is flagrant violation of Clause 27.2.6 of the Certified Standing Order of the BCCL which 
says that no order of discharge or dismissal from service shall be made by an authority lower than the appointing 
authority of the workman. In this regard though the management has submitted that this can be done in case of 
delegated power but it is relevant to mention that the management has failed to produce any document regarding 
delegation of power in support of his submission and for this reason also the dismissal order suffers from serious 
illegality and is liable to be set aside. 


21. Thus on the basis of the above discussions of facts, circumstances and materials available on the case 
record this Tribunal finds and holds that the dismissal order dated 24.06/03.07.2010 suffers from illegality and is 
hereby set aside and the action of the management of Lodna Colliery of M/s BCCL in dismissing Shri Anil Kumar 
Paswan, Ex-SDL Mazdoor from the services of the company vide order dated 03.07.2010 is neither justified nor fair 
and the workman is entitled to reinstatement. Accordingly the management is directed to reinstate the services of the 
workman shri Anil Kumar Paswan within a period of 3 months from the date of the publication of the Award. The

This claim petition is filed by the Petitioner u/s.2A(3) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 directly seeking relief

10.10.2018 is unjustified and further direct the Respondent/Management to pay full back wages, continuity of

2. As per the claim statement, the Petitioner joined the service of the Respondent Bank at Ulundhurpet

3. The Respondent/Management issued an order of suspension dated 20.03.2018 alleging the Petitioner that he 
committed an act of misappropriation and an enquiry was initiated. Although, the Petitioner has taken responsibility 
for loss of money in currency chest and paid a sum of Rs.3,500/- on 14.03.2018, Rs.47,300/- on 19.03.2018 and 
Rs.5000/- on 07.04.2018. According to the Petitioner, the management has assured him that he will be allowed to 
retire on attaining the age of superannuation on 30.06.2018. The Respondent Bank issued charge sheet dated 
25.06.2018, wherein it is alleged that the Petitioner has fraudulently misappropriated soiled notes to the tune of 
Rs.51,400/- and thereafter, remitted the same amount and thus, he acted in a manner prejudicial to the interest of the 
bank. Since the Petitioner was at the verge of retirement and he has to depend on his terminal benefits and the 
Respondent has also assured him that if he remits the amount allegedly lost from the currency chest by submitting 
letter as per dictates to the management, he will be allowed to retire otherwise he will be thrown out of employment.

qs The Disciplinary Authority vide its letter No.RO/VIG//2018-2019 dated 18.04.2018 noticed the petitioner

9. The Petitioner has confined his argument to the extent that punishment imposed by the 
Respondent/Management is disproportionate to the charges leveled against him and therefore, this Tribunal must 
invoke its powers provided under section 110 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The Petitioner challenged the 
validity of domestic enquiry conducted by the Respondent/Management and this Tribunal vide its order dated 
08.09.2025 decided the issue of fairness of enquiry against the Petitioner. It is argued on behalf of the Petitioner that 
this Court by invoking its power u/s.11A of the Act may interfere with the punishment of dismissal from service. It 
is argued that section 110 ofthe Act this Tribunal is empowered to — 


a) Re-appreciate the evidence relied on in the domestic enquiry 

b) Determine whether findings are supported by evidence; 

०) Examine whether the punishment is justified and proportionate; 

d) May substitute a lesser punishment, if the punishment imposed is excessive. 

10. It is argued on behalf of the Petitioner that Petitioner has educated only in Tamil medium and enquiry was 


conducted in English language. The charges alleged against the Petitioner were false and baseless. The Petitioner 
was assured if the alleged cash shortage | was remitted and letter was signed, he would be permitted to retire 
peacefully and thus, the Petitioner has remitted the amount only under compulsion and under expectation that his 
terminal benefits would not be denied. It is also argued that no criminal case was registered against the Petitioner 
and the Petitioner has completed 34 years of unblemished service with the Respondent Bank and the Respondent 
Bank failed to consider the past records of the Petitioner. The punishment of dismissal from service is highly unfair, 
unreasonable and disproportionate to the alleged charges made against the Petitioner. 


11. In contra, it is argued on behalf of the Respondent/Management _ that the Petitioner has misappropriated 
the currency notes of the bank; he admitted his guilt in writing and failed to provide any evidence in his defense. 
The CCTV footage confirmed the guilt wherein it is seen that the Petitioner has taken out the currency from his pant 
pocket and kept on the floor and pushed them under the Almirah. It is also argued that misappropriation of money is a 
serious offence and the Respondent Bank lost its faith reposed on the Petitioner. Therefore, the order of dismissal is 
appropriate and there is no occasion to interfere with the punishment awarded by the Respondent/Management by 
invoking the provisions of section 11A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. 


12. It appears that the Petitioner was placed under suspension pending investigation of the case in terms of clause 
3(a) read with Clause 12(b) of Memorandum of Settlement dated 10.04.2002 entered into between the Indian Bank 
Association and the workmen Union. The reason of suspension was mentioned in the suspension order and the 
investigation was initiated in terms of the Memorandum of Settlement carried out by the Respondent/Management 
and the workmen Union. Therefore, there is no illegality in issuance of suspension order against the Petitioner. The 
Petitioner has submitted his confession letter dated 15.03.2018 written in Tamil language. The Petitioner has 
admitted in this letter that he misappropriated the total amount of Rs.55,000/- on various occasions. The Petitioner 
himself submitted in reply to the charge sheet issued to the Petitioner that he deposited Rs.3,500/- on 14.03.2018, 
Rs.47,300/- on 19.03.2018 and Rs.5000/- on 07.04.2018. It is now argued that this letter was written under coercion. 
But, this fact of coercion is not available on record. The amount is deposited by the Petitioner himself and he 
admitted this fact in his letter dated 04.05.2018 available at page 5 of the paper book of the respondent. 


13. The Petitioner was charged with three Articles of Charge- 
Having regard to the above Statement of Allegation, it is charged that 


i) You had dishonestly and fraudulently removed currencies from Rs.100/- soiled note sections from Currency 
Chest as detailed in the above allegation and misappropriated p the Cash for your personal pecuniary benefit. 
Thereby you had acted in a manner prejudicial to the interest of the Bank, 


9952 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : AUGUST 29, 2026/ BHADRA 7, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


ii) you had breached the trust reposed by the Bank in as much as a Clerk/Shroff of Currency Chest, you had 
committed the above act of misappropriation. 


iii) You had acted in manner unbecoming of an employee of a financial institution and you had violated the 
instructions contained in Para 9.1 under Section B Chapter A 1 Volume 4 of Bank's Book of Instructions in as 
much as while segregating currencies and preparing sections into soiled/cut and re-issuable notes, you had 
misappropriated the amount as detailed in the above allegation to obtain undue personal pecuniary gains to 
yourself. 


14. After receiving copy of charge sheet dated 25.06.2018, the Petitioner has written a letter to the Enquiry 
Officer on 26.06.2018 (page 9 of the paper book). The relevant part of the letter runs as under:- 


“T admit all the allegations and articles of charges mentioned in the charge sheet dated 25.06.2018. I request the EO 
to conduct enquiry on 27.06.2018 and complete the proceedings and I have gone through the list of documents and I 
have nothing more to offer. 


I do not propose to have a defense representative; 
I request the EO to conduct enquiry as requested and dispose of at the earliest. 


This letter was written in English language and was signed by the Petitioner in English language. 


15. During the enquiry proceedings, the delinquent employee admitted that he has received charge sheet dated 
25.06.2018 and he admitted that he understood the charges framed against him. Although, the Enquiry Officer read 
out charges again in front of the delinquent employee and he accepted all the charges levelled in the charge sheet 
dated 25.06.2018 unconditionally . The Enquiry Officer proceeded with the enquiry in spite the delinquent employee 
accepting all the charges voluntarily and unconditionally. The Presenting Officer submitted list of documents and 
witnesses proposed to rely upon by the Management. He submitted two CDs containing of CCTV footage of 
currency chest, investigation report made by R.Velan, Vigilance Office, R.O., Puducherry. The confession letter 
written by the Petitioner dated 15.03.2008 and the branch credit cash voucher dated 18.03.2018, 07.04.2018 for 
Rs.47,300/- and Rs.5000/- respectively. These documents were marked as Ex.ME1 to ME8. The Enquiry Officer 
provided an opportunity to the Petitioner and asked him have you gone through management documents provided 
along with Enquiry Officer letter dated 26.06.2018. The Petitioner answered in positive and accepted all the charges 
voluntarily and unconditionally. The Enquiry Officer again provided an opportunity to go through the documents 
provided by the management . During the enquiry, the Petitioner again admitted the charges voluntarily and 
unconditionally knowing consequences arising out of admission of guilt. The Petitioner denied to produce any 
witness or document in his defense and requested to waive of his defense. 


16. As per discussion above, the concerned employee admitted the guilt at the earlier stage in reply to charge 
sheet and at the time of enquiry proceedings, the employer was holding disciplinary proceedings in spite of absolute 
admission of guilt and the employee was provided again to defend himself. But, the Petitioner failed to submit 
any oral or documentary evidence before the Enquiry Officer although criminal prosecution was not initiated by 
the Respondent/Management, but that omission cannot wash out admission of guilt of delinquent employee and the 
evidence of CCTV footage and enquiry report submitted by the Investigation Officer in the departmental 
proceedings. The admission of guilt by the Petitioner appears voluntarily and the grounds raised by the Petitioner 
appears to be an afterthought and based on legal advise that this admission was made under duress or coercion 
or threat. 


17. Now I have to consider whether punishment imposed on the Petitioner is shockingly disproportionate? 


18. Admittedly, the Respondent Bank had lost its faith reposed on the Petitioner and the act of 
misappropriation committed by the Petitioner is grievous misconduct 


19. In a case law in Municipal Committee, Bahadurgarh v. Krishnan Behari and others, (1996) 2 LLN 
881,wherein it was observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that act of misappropriation is relevant and the amount 
of misappropriation may be small or large. In a case of such nature, indeed, in cases involving corruption there 
cannot be any other punishment than dismissal. Any sympathy shown in such cases is totally uncalled for and 
opposed to public interest. 


20. In view of the above discussion, in my view, the impugned order passed by the Respondent/Management is 
valid and I am not inclined to interfere with the punishment of dismissal from service imposed by the 
Respondent/Management on the Petitioner u/s.11A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

AWARD 


Matter placed today before Tribunal for order. perused the record. This industrial dispute was received 
from Government of India, Ministry of Labour by its order No. L-12012/250/2001-IR(B.I) dated 21.11.2001, 
which has been referred under section 10(1)(d) of the I.D. Act, 1947 for adjudication with the following terms:- 


THE SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of State Bank of India, Tirupathi Zone in dismissing the services 
of Sri J. Ananda Rao, Ex-Messenger, is justified? If not, what relief the workman is entitled?” 


After receipt of the reference, it was numbered as ID No. 22/2002 and notices were issued to both the Workman and 
the management. 


2. The perusal of the claim statement filed by the Petitioner as well as the counter of the Respondent goes to 
reveal that this matter pertains to the termination of the Petitioner from service by the Respondent. The Appropriate 
government has not referred any industrial dispute to this Tribunal for adjudication in respect of termination of 
Petitioner. 


Section 10 (4) provides:- 


“10(4):-Where in an order referring an industrial dispute to [a Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal] under 
this section or in a subsequent order, the appropriate Government has specified the points of dispute for adjudication, 
[the Labour Court or the Tribunal or the National Tribunal, as the case may be,] shall confine its adjudication to 
those points and matters incidental thereto.” 


Thus, in view of the above provision the Industrial Tribunal cannot decide a dispute not explicitly referred to it by the 
appropriate Government as it’s jurisdiction under Section 10 (4) of ID Act, 1947 is confined to the specific point of 
dispute mentioned in the reference order and matter incidental there to. If the reference is for dismissal but the matter 
pertains to the termination, the Tribunal must strictly stick to the referred terms. 


3. Therefore, in view of the provision contained under Section 10(4) of the I.D.Act, 1947, there is no reference 
of the industrial dispute regarding termination of the Petitioner for adjudication before this Tribunal. The reference of 
dispute herein pertain to the dismissal of the Petitioner from service. Therefore, this Tribunal cannot adjudicate the 
dispute in the absence of reference of termination by retrenchment of Petitioner. Thus, Reference is answered 
accordingly. 


Award is passed accordingly. Transmit.

2. इसके द्वारा यह सूचित किया जाता है कि कम्पनी अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 248 (2) के तहत कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार को उपर्युक्त 
कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार 
आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी 
अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रूप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने 
का अनुरोध किया है। 

3. तदनुसार, कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार उपर्युक्त कम्पनियों के नामों को कम्पनियों के रजिस्टर से हटाने का प्रस्ताव करता है। 

4. यदि किसी व्यक्ति/संस्था को कम्पनी को कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से कम्पनियों का नाम हटाने के प्रस्ताव से आपत्ति है तो वह व्यक्ति/संस्था 
इस सूचना के प्रकाशन की तारीख से 30 (तीस) दिनों के भीतर उपर्युक्त कार्यालय के पते पर अपनी आपत्ति भेज सकते हैं |

कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार

2. इसके द्वारा यह सूचित किया जाता है कि कम्पनी अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 248 (2) के तहत कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार को उपर्युक्त 


कम्पनियों के नाम कम्पनी रजिस्टर से इस आधार पर नाम हटाने का आवेदन प्राप्त हुआ है कि कम्पनी के निगमन के एक वर्ष के भीतर कारोबार 
आरंभ करने में विफल रहे हैं या इस आधार पर कि कम्पनी पूर्ववर्ती 2 वित्तीय वर्षों से कारोबार नहीं कर पाई है और इस अवधि के भीतर कम्पनी 
अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 455 के तहत निष्क्रिय कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त करने का आदेश का आवेदन नहीं किया है या कम्पनी ने निष्क्रिय 
कम्पनी की स्थिति प्राप्त कर ली है, पर वे कम्पनी के रूप में पंजीकरण नहीं रखना चाहते और अतः कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से अपना/अपने नाम हटाने 


का अनुरोध किया है। 
3. तदनुसार, कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार उपर्युक्त कम्पनियों के नामों को कम्पनियों के रजिस्टर से हटाने का प्रस्ताव करता है। 
4. यदि किसी व्यक्ति/संस्था को कम्पनी को कम्पनी रजिस्ट्रार से कम्पनियों का नाम हटाने के प्रस्ताव से आपत्ति है तो वह व्यक्ति/संस्था 
इस सूचना के प्रकाशन की तारीख से 30 (तीस) दिनों के भीतर उपर्युक्त कार्यालय के पते पर अपनी आपत्ति भेज सकते हैं |
